clause.notes: Added because every case in this cluster ships a MISSING traffic_advisory whose identifier was minted so the absence itself could be cited, and every one carries a driver assertion of an external traffic cause - the CTE queue at Braddell in case 508, the Balestier bus breakdown in 530, the KPE signal loss in 110, the 'app acting up' in 112, the hung phone in 512 and the unaccounted telemetry gap in 9115. POL-RD-08 already provides that an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's burden, but POL-RD-10(5) lists 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' among its escalation triggers, so the same facts read one way pay a POL-RD-02 refund and read the other way escalate with no money moving. The human closures in this cluster settled the point: 508 and 530 were decided as established deviations with the ordinary POL-RD-02 refund, the absent advisory making the driver's excuse weightless under POL-RD-08 and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. This clause states that priority for the whole cluster and leaves POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) untouched for cases 110, 112, 512 and 9115, where the trace itself is impaired and the missing advisory is not the deciding defect.
clause.rule: Where a party asserts an external traffic cause - a queue, a breakdown, a closure or an incident - as the explanation for a measured route deviation, the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory record that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the gps_trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and is matched by a route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. Where the bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering the trip window - the artifact's admissibility status is MISSING and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 - that comparison cannot be run on the record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Two consequences follow, and no others. (1) Where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is NOT an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. This clause does not narrow POL-RD-10(5) where the party does cite the missing identifier; that case still escalates. (2) Where the rider has shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold on a gps_trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route; the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and the ruling must record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file. This clause does not displace POL-RD-07: where the gps_trace IS impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists, POL-RD-10(3) still governs and the case still escalates.
